component.name: udev-rule-generator
udev-rule-generator
component.summary: Habilitar joysticks y gamepads con reglas udev
Enable joysticks and gamepads with udev rules

description.p: udev-rule-generator es una herramienta para Linux que detecta los joysticks y gamepads conectados y crea reglas en /etc/udev/rules.d para habilitar su uso.
Permite generar una regla para un mando concreto y activar, de forma opcional, las reglas de Steam/SteamVR de Valve y game-devices-udev de Fabian Bornschein. No se instalan por defecto.

ul.li: Detección de mandos USB y Bluetooth con udevadm.
Reglas de permiso con MODE 0660 y TAG uaccess.
Detección automática al conectar un mando y notificaciones de GNOME.
Dispositivos guardados para activar o desactivar sus reglas sin conectarlos.
Ocultar dispositivos guardados y recuperarlos desde el menú Dispositivos ocultos.
Instalación con el diálogo de autenticación de polkit de GNOME.
Interfaz de terminal y aplicación GTK4/libadwaita.

description.p: udev-rule-generator is a Linux tool that detects connected joysticks and gamepads and creates rules in /etc/udev/rules.d to enable their use.
It can generate a rule for a specific controller and optionally enable Valve's Steam/SteamVR rules and Fabian Bornschein's game-devices-udev rules. They are not installed by default.

ul.li: USB and Bluetooth controller detection with udevadm.
Permission rules with MODE 0660 and the uaccess tag.
Automatic detection when a controller is connected and GNOME notifications.
Saved devices whose rules can be enabled or disabled without connecting them.
Hide saved devices and restore them from the Hidden devices menu.
Installation through the GNOME polkit authentication dialog.

description.p: Shows the active js node in the subtitle of connected devices.
Fixes game-devices-udev install filenames to use the required 71- prefix.
Replaces the steam-devices description with a red uinput warning when the kernel module is unavailable.
Shows a red warning when uinput is unavailable and keeps the steam-devices switch disabled.

Adds the optional game-devices-udev package from Fabian Bornschein (fabiscafe) below steam-devices in External rules, with the same enable/disable workflow and CLI support. The steam-devices switch is disabled when the uinput kernel module is unavailable.
First production release: primary GTK4/libadwaita GUI, matching CLI, enabled/disabled device rules, hidden devices, validated steam-devices presets, and English/Spanish localization.
Lists saved but disconnected devices in the CLI, fixes reopening the hidden-devices window, and keeps ignore rules removed.

Removes ignore rules; saved devices now have only enabled and disabled states. Shows saved but disconnected devices in the CLI, fixes reopening the hidden-devices window, and validates downloaded and bundled Steam rules.
Removes the Ignorar dispositivos section and fake-joystick detection. Adds an eye button to hide saved devices and a Hidden devices menu to restore them.
Adds a trash button to saved Ignorar dispositivos rows so a saved record and its active ignore rule can be removed.
Merges js devices found only in /proc, reads capabilities from /sys as a fallback, and shows probable fake joysticks even when an old allow rule is saved.
Detects probable fake joysticks from evdev capabilities instead of matching device names or VID:PID values, and exposes that detection in the Ignorar dispositivos section.
Removes the former vendor preset library, keeps only steam-devices, moves its switch into the main window, and adds an Ignorar dispositivos section for probable fake joysticks.
Batches device switch changes behind an Apply changes button so a group of rule installs and removals uses one polkit authentication. Also fixes the Ctrl+C shutdown hang.
New generated rule filenames include the application name, for example 10-udev-rule-generator-gamepad-…. Existing rules are renamed when they are disabled and enabled again or reinstalled.
Removes the Enable all switch, simplifies the device list description, and fixes the About dialog crash. The app continues to use pkexec/polkit and never stores the password.
Removes hidden devices and the Configure dialog. Connected controllers without a saved rule can be added directly with their switch. Fixes the About dialog and simplifies the device rows.
Makes saved-device management the main window, with per-device switches, active and disabled counts, an Enable all switch, green Connected tags, and Configure actions for connected controllers.

Removes the redundant refresh buttons, aligns card borders, and simplifies the presets dialog by removing counts, the subtitle, the license group, and switch subtitles while adding the upstream repository URLs to the descriptions.

Makes every device row a separate card for consistent shadows, removes the duplicate device-information group from the configuration dialog, removes the intro block from the presets dialog, refreshes silently without flashing the loading page, and removes the redundant controller-count subtitle.
Shows separate green and gray counts for active and disabled saved rules, renames the section to Manage devices, and removes the redundant gamepad avatar icons from device rows.
Removes the duplicate close button from dialogs and renames the default action to Enable (default), while keeping the underlying udev action as allow.
Prints a short startup message with the app version and a final Closing message, so running from the terminal or Flatpak is not silent.
Grants the Flatpak GPU device permission, so GTK can use hardware acceleration and Mesa no longer reports missing DRI/Zink devices.
Handles Ctrl+C gracefully: stops the udev monitor, timers, and worker executor, then exits without a Python traceback.
Removes the empty gap between the controller list and the lower sections by scrolling the whole page as one column. Managed rules are now detected from the marker on their first line.

Simplifies the header menu to Hidden devices and About, keeps a single Installed rules row in Status for the saved-device switches, and adds an External rules section for the optional Valve and fabiscafe packages.
Removes the rule preview from the device dialog and adds an Enable all switch to Saved devices. The switch enables only inactive devices and leaves rules that are already active untouched.
Makes generated rule files easier to read: only the app version, a blank line, the device name, and the rule lines. The app still uses one file per controller, so each file has one device block.

Adds a JSON registry of saved devices with their latest generated rule. Existing managed rules are imported automatically, and each saved rule can be enabled or disabled from the GUI or the new --known/--enable-known/--disable-known CLI options without plugging in the controller.
Adds tools/update_presets.py to refresh bundled rules from Codeberg and GitHub, and links the README to the upstream projects and author.
Stops writing the transient /dev/input node list in generated rule headers. New rules no longer include a Nodos/Nodes comment.
Changes the language fallback for unsupported locales to English and makes the website follow system light/dark theme changes.
Usa udev-rule-generator como nombre visible en todos lados y muestra el número de reglas administradas como un tag en Reglas instaladas.
Los presets se eligen por paquete completo: game-devices-udev (fabiscafe) o steam-devices (Valve). Elimina el selector de fabricantes y la separación entre Steam Input y SteamVR.
Elimina la fila de estado “Detección automática” y el preset especial de Microsoft Xbox. Los presets quedan limitados a la biblioteca de fabiscafe y a steam-devices.
Deja los presets únicamente con game-devices-udev (fabiscafe) y steam-devices (Valve). Elimina el preset local de hardware específico y las líneas locales de un modelo Xbox.
Añade autodetección de idioma español/inglés (en_US/en_GB), traduce la interfaz, la CLI y las reglas generadas, y arregla el pie del diálogo para que el texto largo no tape los botones.
Centra el icono de los dispositivos, añade la opción de ocultarlos y un diálogo de Dispositivos ocultos con botón para desocultarlos.
Añade el argumento --gui a udev-rule-generator para abrir la interfaz gráfica desde el mismo lanzador de terminal.
La GUI detecta automáticamente la conexión y desconexión de mandos, envía notificaciones de GNOME y usa una vista de tarjetas centradas al estilo de Pika Backup.
Añade las reglas opcionales de steam-devices (Steam Input y SteamVR), separa los presets opcionales de las reglas recomendadas y deja todas las fuentes opcionales desactivadas por defecto.
Primera versión: detección, reglas de permitir/ignorar, presets y GUI.
